# Decisions — Regional view

Decision records moved verbatim from the root `CLAUDE.md`, whose index
lists every decision number and where it lives. Numbers are stable;
"decision N" anywhere in the notes resolves through that index.

Decisions: 21.

21. **The Regional view is a READ-ONLY ROLLUP, and it nests by ROSETTE**
    (`core/overview.dart`, `app/overview_map.dart`). A third view beside Hex
    and Sketch (`MainView` in `main.dart` replaced the old `_sketchMode`
    bool), showing the same campaign at ~21-mile hexes. Distance measurement
    itself was already built — the ruler tool and the scale bar are decision
    18 — and the regional view feeds them its own [MapScale], so both read
    real-world miles at either scale with no second code path.
    - **7, not 8.** A hexagon cannot be cut into 8 congruent hexagons: an
      exact hex-of-hexes nests only by 3, 7, 19… "3-mile detail, 24-mile
      regional" therefore has no exact form, and the classic hexcrawl answer
      is the ROSETTE — a centre plus its six neighbours. Two levels is 49
      detail hexes and `sqrt(7)^2 = 7` hex-widths exactly, so 3-mile hexes
      give **21-mile** regional ones: as close to 24 as an exact tiling comes,
      and the trade is deliberate. The alternative (scale the lattice by 8 and
      assign each detail centre to its nearest big hex) hits the round number
      but makes membership depend on where the origin sits, so a hex's own
      neighbours can land in different parents.
    - **The tiling is the sublattice generated by `(3,-1)` and `(1,2)`** —
      determinant 7, which is exactly why 7 is available and 8 is not.
      `rosetteOf` is its exact integer inverse (`a = (2q-r)/7`, `b = (q+3r)/7`
      each rounded to the nearest multiple of 7); the rounding regions ARE the
      tiles, which is why no gap or overlap is possible rather than merely
      unobserved. `overview_test.dart` asserts the partition directly: every
      cell within distance 1 of its centre, every rosette exactly 7 distinct
      members, no cell claimed twice, and a round trip at two levels.
    - **A regional hex contains NOTHING of its own** — no file, no name, no
      page, no terrain. Fill (majority biome), stamp (top feature by
      `featurePriority` — one hex has room for one stamp) and badge (count of
      keyed hexes) are all derived on read. That is what makes the two scales
      unable to disagree and means there is no migration, ever. Everything a
      GM writes stays at hexcrawl scale, and Ctrl+Z is refused here with a
      message rather than silently editing a map that is not on screen (the
      same reasoning as decision 19's separate sketch stack).
    - **Coverage is shown, not hidden.** A part-drawn cell fades toward
      `emptyFill` in proportion to how much of it is painted: at 21 miles the
      honest signal is "there is not much here yet", and a full-strength fill
      derived from three painted hexes out of 49 would claim otherwise. Cells
      OUTSIDE the grid window are not counted at all, so a regional hex on the
      map edge reports coverage over the part that exists.
    - **Ties break toward the rosette's CENTRE cell**, then by enum order —
      stable, so a campaign always renders identically.
    - **`overviewWindow` maps the campaign's grid window up into the regional
      lattice**, because the regional lattice has no window of its own. It
      scans only the detail window's per-column top and bottom (a rosette is
      convex and monotone in `q` and in `unstaggeredRow`, so the extremes are
      on the boundary) and pads by a ring; the test asserts containment for
      every detail cell across five window shapes, including negative `minQ`
      and a non-zero `rShift`.
    - **Badges are scene-scaled with a screen-pixel FLOOR**, not one or the
      other. Pinned to screen pixels a badge is a speck beside a hex filling
      half the window; pinned to scene units it vanishes when zoomed out.
      (While checking this: `TextPainter` in `flutter test` renders every
      glyph as a solid box of uniform width — `"1"` is as wide as it is tall —
      so a digit in a rendered PNG looks like a filled rectangle. That is the
      headless test font, not a bug. Don't chase it.)
    - **The camera is handed across as the DETAIL camera** and converted on
      the way in and out (`overviewZoom`), so `MainView` switching does not
      need to know about the sqrt(7) factor — the conversion lives entirely
      inside the view and round-trips as the identity.
    - **The toolbar's centre group is now horizontally scrollable.** Adding a
      third view segment overflowed the `Row` by 2 px at the app's minimum
      width — caught by the existing shell smoke tests, and the next tool
      would have done it again.
